nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaches the forest floor only in patches under the tall canopy, so understory plants rely on gaps and edges.

nodes.name: Coastal summer fog
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says fog supplies a large share of the water redwoods use, and that its summer consistency matters more to tree health than rainfall.

nodes.name: Winter rain
nodes.desc: Heavy rain on the Pacific coast feeds streams and the temperate rainforest. Fog covers much of the dry summer.

nodes.name: Forest soil and fallen logs
nodes.desc: Fallen redwoods hold moisture and slowly return nutrients to the soil, and act as nursery sites for seedlings and homes for salamanders.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen trees, leaf litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Coast redwood
nodes.desc: The tallest tree on Earth. It takes up fog water through its leaves and bark, and its canopy builds soil that holds life high above ground.

nodes.name: Sitka spruce
nodes.desc: A conifer of the foggy coast that grows beside redwoods. Elk browse it and Douglas squirrels eat its seeds, per GloBI records.

nodes.name: Salmonberry
nodes.desc: A berry-bearing understory shrub. Elk and deer browse it, and bears and birds eat the fruit.

nodes.name: Salal
nodes.desc: An evergreen understory shrub with berries. Deer, elk, band-tailed pigeons and bears feed on it.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: The large mammal most often seen in the parks. Eats grasses, ferns, shrubs and berries, and is prey for cougars and black bears.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs, ferns and bracken in the understory. A main prey of cougars, and its carcasses feed scavengers.

nodes.name: Douglas squirrel
nodes.desc: A small tree squirrel that eats conifer seeds, including those of Sitka spruce per GloBI.

nodes.name: Brush rabbit
nodes.desc: Eats plants and, per Wikipedia, preys on young redwood seedlings. Prey for foxes and cougars.

nodes.name: Pacific banana slug
nodes.desc: A big forest-floor slug that eats leaves, moss, dung and dead plant matter, and recycles them into soil. Snakes and small mammals sometimes eat it.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small omnivore of seeds, fruit and insects. A common prey of snakes and foxes.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: A small canid that hunts mice, rabbits and shrew moles, per GloBI.

nodes.name: Common garter snake
nodes.desc: Eats rodents and frogs in GloBI records. Wikipedia notes snakes sometimes eat banana slugs.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever scavenger that feeds on carrion, among much else.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds and eats carcasses, including deer in GloBI records.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Mostly eats plants such as berries but also hunts elk and deer calves and scavenges carrion. Fishes for salmon on the coast.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: Hunts mainly deer and elk. Bears and scavengers often take over its kills.
